question: Does fading the first touch of a 09:30 GEX PRO level make money out of sample, after slippage and fees? Every trade is hypothetical: no order is ever placed.
sessions: every (date, market) with a graded track-record plan (levels, expected move and the 09:30 ratio, read exactly as studies/level_reaction/v2.json reads them) and an archive day holding that market's futures 1-minute bars ({M}F-1m.json, Yahoo Finance) with no A2 or A3 violation. RTH bars only: bar start in [the day's 09:30 ET, its close) from gexsys/marketcal.py. A day without archive bars is left out and named.
trigger: the touch of studies/level_reaction/v2.json (same tol, side, at_open, gap_through, no_prior_close and cluster rules) found on the archive bars' highs and lows; level types ZG CW PW Ab1 C1-C3 P1-P3; dependent levels and every non-touch category never trigger
side: fade: short when the level is above the open, long when it is below
one_position: per market and grid point, one position at a time: a trigger whose bar starts before the open trade's exit bar is skipped; triggers in time order, ties in the level-type order above
entry: the open of the bar after the trigger bar, 1 tick against us (long +1 tick, short -1 tick); no later RTH bar: no trade
stop: short: level + s x tol; long: level - s x tol. An entry at or beyond the stop is no trade (counted)
target: short: entry - t x R; long: entry + t x R

exits.order: bar by bar from the entry bar: first the time exit, then the stop, then the target
exits.time: the first bar starting at or after entry minute + T: exit at its open, 1 tick against us
exits.stop: high >= stop (short) or low <= stop (long): exit at the worse of the stop and that bar's open, 1 tick against us
exits.target: low <= target (short) or high >= target (long): exit at the target, 1 tick against us, never better even on a gap
exits.same_bar: stop and target inside one bar: the stop
exits.close: flat by the close: no exit by the last RTH bar: exit at its close, 1 tick against us

units.fees_note: configurable (--fees); the amount is shown with every result

per_trade: points and R after slippage, before fees; dollars per 1 contract after slippage and fees

walk_forward.window: expanding, per market, sessions in date order
walk_forward.why_20: the 8 grid points are ranked on in-sample trades; the level touch rate is about 1 per session per market (studies/level_reaction v2, Oct 21 - Nov 18: 21 counted touches in 21 sessions each), so 20 sessions give about 20 trades to rank them on. Fewer makes the choice noise; the same minimum as the splits study's groups
walk_forward.choice: for each k >= 20: the grid point with the highest mean net dollars per trade over sessions 1..k (ties and no trades at all: the first in grid order); it trades session k+1
walk_forward.reported: only the stitched sessions k+1; no session used for tuning is ever scored

in_sample_vs_out: for each out-of-sample session, the chosen grid point's in-sample mean R per trade; their mean is shown beside the out-of-sample mean R per trade (the gap is the overfitting warning)
not_enough_data: fewer than 30 out-of-sample trades: no statistic is shown, only 'not enough data' with the trade and session counts
uncertainty: expectancy per trade and per session over out-of-sample sessions with gexpro/uncertainty.py (95% expanded percentile or BCa, 10,000 whole-session resamples, seed 20261118, p-value against 0, sessions needed labelled optimistic)
equity_band: cumulative net dollars by out-of-sample session; 10,000 resamples of those sessions with replacement, seed 20261118; the 2.5% and 97.5% values at each session count
drawdown_and_streak: maximum peak-to-trough fall of cumulative net dollars by trade; longest run of trades with net dollars < 0; win = net dollars > 0; average win and loss in dollars and R
tries: studies/rules/tries.json lists every rule version and its grid points, appended, never edited; the p-value is also shown adjusted for every grid point tried to date: min(1, p x tries)
roll_weeks: the archive's roll_week flag; results shown with and without roll-week sessions
shift: the expectancy per trade is also shown with every level shifted +5 / -5 points (NQ) and +1 / -1 (ES)
look_ahead: levels, ratio and expected move are frozen before 09:30 (L1, L5); the parameters for session k+1 come only from sessions 1..k; tools/stress/lookahead_audit.py L9 recomputes every choice from earlier sessions only
